findings.finding: On the 21 July call management guided Q3 net interest margin to about 3.45%, down from 3.52% reported in Q2, on rising deposit costs, with improvement expected in Q4; the Fed then raised the funds rate 25 bp on 16 September (first hike in over three years, 12-0), after that guide was given and against management's Q1 stance 'We are flat, not assuming up or down', so the Q4 improvement the market holds rests on a rate assumption that has since moved against it, while the $0.96 consensus sits flat on Q2's $0.96.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two prints (2026-07-20 +1.95%, 2026-04-20 +0.90%) each carried a margin outlook and moved inside the deadband; the two largest reactions in the baseline (2025-01-21 +8.08%, 2025-04-21 +6.70%) came when the margin surprised upward after rate cuts lowered funding costs.
findings.why_not_priced: The 3.45% guide is priced (consensus EPS flat QoQ matches it); what is not is whether the Q4 'improvement' survives a hike the guide did not assume. If the market had repriced the Q4 outlook the consensus would have moved below Q2's $0.96 and the targets would have come down; instead Benchmark raised to $60 in August and the stock only drifted 2.6% over 20 sessions.
findings.independence: The Q3 guide is reported identically by two aggregators of the call (https://quartr.com/events/smartfinancial-inc-smbk-q2-2026_ofek26C3 and https://in.investing.com/equities/smartfinancial-inc); management's rate stance is quoted from the Q1 transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/04/20/smartfinancial-smbk-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/), where the Q1 margin gain was attributed to rate cuts lowering funding costs, which is the mechanism a hike reverses. No full Q2 transcript was reachable, so the 3.45% figure rests on two summaries, not the primary text.

findings.finding: FB Financial (FirstBank, Nashville; same Tennessee/Alabama deposit market), reporting 13 October, printed Q3 NIM of 3.83% against 3.95% in Q2, a 12 bp compression it attributed to 'higher funding costs relative to earning asset yields', with cost of total deposits up to 2.32% from 2.26% and interest-bearing deposits to 2.88% from 2.81%, and a revenue miss ($174.5M vs $181.6M consensus); SmartFinancial guided only 7 bp of compression in the same market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SMBK's margin has beaten its own guide in the last two quarters (Q1 guided roughly flat, printed +10 bp; Q2 printed 3.52% after a 'slightly up' second-half guide), so a peer's compression has not translated one for one; FBK itself rose about 1.3% pre-market on its miss.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer's print landed after SMBK last spoke and the SMBK consensus did not move on it (still $0.96, no estimate revision found in any source searched); if it had, the revenue bar would sit at or below the guide rather than 1.4% above it.
findings.independence: This is a proxy, not SmartFinancial's number. It points the same way as the company's own Q2 statement that loan growth outran deposit production and $106M of short-term brokered deposits were used (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001038773/000110465926085102/smbk-20260720xex99d1.htm). Finviz's secondary piece on the miss: https://finviz.com/news/401729/fb-financial-reports-third-quarter-eps-in-line-with-estimates-as-revenue-misses-forecasts.

findings.finding: Three other Southeast banks that reported since SMBK last spoke printed margins flat to up: Home BancShares (15 October) core NIM 4.50%, +3 bp QoQ with the rate paid on interest-bearing deposits down to 2.37% from 2.39%; Regions (16 October) NIM 3.68% vs 3.66%; First Horizon (15 October) NIM 3.48%, -1 bp; so the deposit-cost squeeze FBK reported is not uniform across the region.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SMBK's two largest up moves (Jan and Apr 2025) came on margin surprises; a margin at or above the 3.45% guide would repeat that line, but the last two margin beats moved the stock under 2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Same logic as the FBK read: these peer prints post-date SMBK's guide and the SMBK consensus has not moved either way since. Both peer findings are proxies and partly offset; filed apart because they are different sources pointing opposite ways, not two readings of one document.
findings.independence: Regions: https://finviz.com/news/403470/regions-reports-earnings-of-611-million-and-eps-of-071-in-3q-2026 (2026-10-16). First Horizon: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036966/000003696626000178/a3q2026earningsrelease.htm (2026-10-15). HOMB and RF are larger and less deposit-constrained than a $5.4B-deposit bank growing loans 15%, so this is a weaker proxy than FBK.

findings.finding: SmartFinancial has beaten consensus in each of the last four prints on record here (Q3 2025 $0.86 vs $0.73, +17.8%; Q2 2026 $0.96 vs a beat flagged by Earnings Whispers; AlphaQuery history), while Q2 carried 15% annualised organic loan growth ($165M, to $4.68B) against management's own '10% plus/minus' framing and a provision of only $1.46M; the Q3 EPS bar of $0.96 is flat on Q2, so balance-sheet growth above the framing is the room to clear it even at the guided margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats are bought but modestly: +2.98% on the Q3 2025 beat of 17.8%, +1.95% on the Q2 2026 beat; 6 of 7 reactions in the baseline are positive with a median absolute move of 2.98%.
findings.why_not_priced: A beat habit is visible to anyone with the history, so most of it is priced; what is not is the size of the loan-growth lever against a bar that assumes none. If priced, consensus would sit above Q2's $0.96 rather than on it after a quarter of 15% annualised growth and a 13% annualised TBV build.
findings.independence: Loan growth, provision and TBV from the company's Q2 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001038773/000110465926085102/smbk-20260720xex99d1.htm, 2026-07-20); the '10% plus/minus' and 'high single-digits-plus' framing from the Q1 transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/04/20/smartfinancial-smbk-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/). This finding and finding 1 are in tension on the level of the bar, not contradictory: one is where the bar sits, the other the company's habit against it.

findings.finding: The Q2 10-Q shows noninterest-bearing demand deposits fell to $921.9M at 30 June 2026 from $1,062.9M at 31 December 2025 (-$141M, about -13%) while time deposits rose to $986.8M from $870.5M, and Q2 loan growth was funded in part with $106M of short-term brokered deposits; the funding mix is shifting toward the costliest deposits going into a quarter whose guide already assumes deposit-cost pressure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print disclosed the brokered usage and the stock rose 1.95%; the market has not punished this line on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It is in a filed 10-Q and inside what the company guided to, so it is largely priced; it is filed small because the mix shift is the mechanism by which a 3.45% guide becomes a miss, and the six-month NIB decline is not in the headline release. The 10-Q's rate-sensitivity table and brokered-deposit note were not readable in the fetched excerpt.
findings.independence: Shares the deposit-cost concern with finding 1 (different document: 10-Q vs the call and the Fed statement) and with the FBK proxy in finding 2. Brokered usage figure from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001038773/000110465926085102/smbk-20260720xex99d1.htm).

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly against the name's own reaction history (6 of 7 up, beats bought) and with the mild 20-session drift down since the Fed hike; with no option skew and no short book there is nothing in positioning to cut against or confirm, and the net is close to a non-result.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (a finding inside what the company already guided is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect): the 10-Q funding-mix finding shrunk from -0.4 to -0.2; the deposit-cost pressure it describes is the premise of the 3.45% guide.
Rule 5 (a proxy is filed small, never left out): the FBK and HOMB/RF/FHN peer reads were already sized as proxies in the draft; left standing.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): consensus $0.96 is sourced to two agreeing estimate pages plus the sweep, so no cap was applied; left standing.
Rule 7 (positioning before any negative): short interest 0.86%, 4.84 days to cover, no skew available; no shrink needed on the negatives; left standing.
Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): p_up was already set near 50 for the beat-bought history; left at 48. Post-lessons sum -0.7 against the frozen -0.9.
